key_insight: EFaaS couples the classical optimizer and QPU as a session-aware serverless workflow to cut TTNS and avoid drift in hybrid variational algorithms.
engineering_relevance: It offers a cloud-native scheduling layer for quantum-classical applications that can improve utilization, latency, and convergence without static hardware reservations.
method: Calibration-aware QPU placement to exploit warm calibration caches and reduce cold-start penalties.
Dual-resource fair queuing to prioritize active iterative loops across CPU and QPU resources.
EF-QuantumFuture speculative execution primitive to overlap classical work with quantum latency.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports TTNS reductions of 11.4%-94.3%, QDC gains of 2.02%-15.78 percentage points, and convergence speedups of 83.2%-98.3% across evaluated baselines.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate session tracking, calibration-state awareness, and scheduler integration with quantum cloud infrastructure, which may be challenging in heterogeneous deployments.
paper_title: EFaaS: A Quantum-Classical Serverless Entangled Scheduler for Hybrid Variational Algorithms
